name: Global Cypher Query Contract
description: Mandatory rules the Cypher agent must apply to EVERY generated query against the Worktual OKG. Retrieve and prepend this card on every request.
business_rules: CASE SENSITIVITY: Neo4j labels, relationship types and property names are case-sensitive. Labels are PascalCase (Conversation, SalesOrder, ContactProfile). Relationship types are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (HAS_ROUTING_ATTEMPT, BELONGS_TO_SEGMENT). Properties are lower_snake_case (created_at, churn_score, total_amount). Never title-case a property, never PascalCase a relationship, never UPPER a label.

NODE KEYS ARE NOT ALWAYS 'id'. Registry: Contact=cdp_id, CustomerScore=cdp_id, ContactPoint=identity_id, Insight=insight_id, Recommendation=recommendation_id, Segment=segment_id, Order=order_id, OrgProfile=organization_id, KnowledgeOrgProfile=organization_id, AssignmentSettings=organization_id, WebchatChannelConfig=channel_config_id, SocialChannelConfig=channel_config_id, Product=id (bigint), PlatformProduct=id (string). Every other label uses id.

ANCHOR BOTH ENDS WITH LABELS. These relationship types are overloaded and reused across unrelated pairs: CONTAINS, HAS_LINE, FOR_PRODUCT, FOR_CONTACT, FOR_OPPORTUNITY, FOR_ACTIVITY, FOR_ACCOUNT, OWNED_BY, CREATED_BY, ASSIGNED_TO, IN_QUEUE, FROM_QUEUE, HANDLED_BY, OFFERED_AGENT, FOLLOWS_HOURS, USES_TEMPLATE, APPROVED_BY. Never write (a)-[:CONTAINS]->(b) without labels on both a and b.

TENANT SCOPE IS THE DATABASE. Each tenant has its own Neo4j database. Do NOT add `WHERE n.organization_id = $organization_id` unless the runtime actually binds $organization_id — an unbound parameter makes Neo4j throw 'Expected parameter(s)' and the agent returns an error instead of an answer.

DATETIME vs DATE. Most timestamps are ZONED DATETIME (UTC) and must be compared with datetime($period_start). But DATE-typed columns must be compared with date($period_start): Invoice.issue_date, Opportunity.expected_close_date, Contact.acquisition_date, Contact.date_of_birth, Holiday.holiday_date, Quote.valid_until. Mixing date and datetime raises a type error.

DURATIONS. Use duration.inSeconds(a, b).seconds for elapsed time. duration.between(a, b).seconds returns ONLY the seconds component (excludes days/months) and silently under-reports any span longer than 24 hours.
ALWAYS BOUND BOTH ENDS OF A PERIOD: `>= datetime($period_start) AND < datetime($period_end)`. A start-only filter makes 'this week' silently mean 'this week and everything after'.
GUARD DIVISION: CASE WHEN total = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE toFloat(numerator)/total END. A bare toFloat(x)/0 returns null and the answer reads as 'unknown'.
EXISTENCE CHECKS: use EXISTS { (c)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(:Transfer) } or COUNT {}. Bare pattern expressions outside WHERE are removed in Neo4j 5.

NEVER INVENT A TENANT FAN-OUT EDGE. The following (Tenant)-[...]->(x) relationships are commented out in core.yaml and DO NOT EXIST in the graph: HAS_CONTACT, HAS_CONTACT_PROFILE, HAS_CONVERSATION, HAS_INTERACTION, HAS_DEAL, HAS_DEAL_ACTIVITY, HAS_COMPANY, HAS_COMPANY_SITE, HAS_QUOTE, HAS_PROPOSAL, HAS_INVOICE, HAS_SALES_ORDER, HAS_CONTRACT, HAS_NOTIFICATION, HAS_MISSED_CONTACT, HAS_SHARED_NOTE, HAS_KNOWLEDGE_DOCUMENT, HAS_QUOTE_TEMPLATE, HAS_PROPOSAL_TEMPLATE, HAS_INVOICE_TEMPLATE. Match the label directly instead: MATCH (d:Opportunity) — not MATCH (:Tenant)-[:HAS_DEAL]->(d:Opportunity), which returns zero rows.

(Contact)-[:PARTICIPATED_IN]->(Conversation) DOES NOT EXIST. Conversations, interactions, activities, insights and recommendations hang off a Contact through synthetic collection nodes. See concept_contact_history.
IF NO CARD MATCHES, SAY SO. Do not improvise labels or relationship types that are absent from these cards.

description: A Contact does not connect directly to its Conversations, Interactions, Activities, Insights or Recommendations. Each hangs off a synthetic collection node keyed by the same cdp_id. Every 'show me everything about customer X' query must go through the collection hop.
disambiguation: This is the ONLY correct path from a person to their history. (Contact)-[:PARTICIPATED_IN]->(Conversation), (Contact)-[:HAS_CONVERSATION]->(Conversation) and (Tenant)-[:HAS_CONVERSATION]->() are all non-existent and return zero rows.

(Contact)-[:HAS_INTERACTIONS]->(InteractionHistory)-[:CONTAINS]->(Interaction)
(Contact)-[:HAS_ACTIVITIES]->(ActivityTimeline)-[:CONTAINS]->(ContactActivity)
(Contact)-[:HAS_INSIGHTS]->(InsightCollection)-[:CONTAINS]->(Insight)

All five collection nodes are keyed by cdp_id, the same value as the Contact.
CONTAINS is overloaded — it is also (Order)-[:CONTAINS]->(Product). Always label both ends.

name: Missed Contacts
description: A contact that was offered to a specific agent and not answered. Materialised as its own MissedContact node with reason, channel, offered_at and missed_at.
disambiguation: Three different things are often called 'missed'. (1) Agent was offered and did not answer -> MissedContact node (THIS card). (2) Routing could not find any agent to offer to -> RoutingAttempt.outcome, see concept_routing_failure. (3) Customer hung up before any agent -> see concept_abandonment_rate. Do not answer a MissedContact question with RoutingAttempt data or the numbers will not reconcile with the Missed Contacts screen in the product.
business_rules: MissedContact is a first-class node (ccass.agent_missed_contacts). Key = id. Do not derive it from RoutingAttempt.
Use missed_at for the event date. offered_at is when the offer went out, acknowledged_at is when the agent cleared it.
Available relationships: (MissedContact)-[:MISSED_BY]->(Agent), -[:ASSIGNED_USER]->(Employee), -[:FROM_CONVERSATION]->(Conversation), -[:FROM_QUEUE]->(Queue), -[:FOR_CONTACT]->(Contact).
There is NO (Tenant)-[:HAS_MISSED_CONTACT]->(MissedContact) edge — match (mc:MissedContact) directly.
Grouping dimensions available directly on the node without a join: channel, reason, customer_name, customer_email, customer_phone.
The Agent-side name is Agent.display_name, not Agent.name.
For 'why did it increase', run the diagnostic_template ONCE — it returns dimension, current, previous, delta in a single pass.
cypher_template: MATCH (mc:MissedContact) WHERE mc.missed_at >= datetime($period_start) AND mc.missed_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(mc) AS missed_count
diagnostic_template: MATCH (mc:MissedContact)-[:FROM_QUEUE]->(q:Queue) WITH q.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN mc.missed_at >= datetime($period_start) AND mc.missed_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN mc.missed_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND mc.missed_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5

name: Routing Failure / No Agent Available
description: Attempts by the router to place a conversation with an agent, and their outcomes. Used for capacity and coverage questions, not for agent-level missed contacts.
disambiguation: This is the routing engine's view. For an agent who was offered and did not answer use concept_missed_contacts. For a customer who left the queue use concept_abandonment_rate.

Use ra.created_at for when the attempt was made and ra.completed_at for when it resolved.
attempt_number lets you separate first offers from retries; count DISTINCT conversations, not attempts, when the question is about contacts rather than offers.

name: Abandonment Rate
description: Share of conversations where the customer disconnected before any agent was assigned.
disambiguation: Customer-side. For agent-side non-answer use concept_missed_contacts; for router-side failure use concept_routing_failure.
business_rules: Abandoned = ended_at IS NOT NULL AND assigned_at IS NULL.
end_reason and end_actor carry the reason; end_actor distinguishes customer-initiated from system-initiated. Discover the values before filtering on them rather than assuming codes.
Denominator is all conversations created in the period. Guard against a zero denominator.
Conversation has NO queue_id property in the graph — group by queue only through (Conversation)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(Queue). Group by channel using the scalar c.channel property, which is always populated.

name: First Contact Resolution (FCR)
description: Conversations resolved without any transfer to another queue or agent.
business_rules: FCR = resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND no (Conversation)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(:Transfer).
Use EXISTS { } for the negation. Bare pattern expressions inside CASE are invalid in Neo4j 5.
Report the rate, not just the count — a raw fcr_count with no denominator is meaningless.

A conversation with CONTINUES_FROM set is a follow-up of a previous contact and arguably not FCR. If the question is about true first-time resolution, exclude them: NOT EXISTS { (c)-[:CONTINUES_FROM]->(:Conversation) }.

name: Average Handle Time (AHT)
description: Average elapsed seconds from agent assignment to resolution.
business_rules: AHT = duration.inSeconds(c.assigned_at, c.resolved_at).seconds. Do NOT use duration.between(...).seconds — it drops the day component and under-reports any conversation open longer than 24 hours, which is common on email.
Only include rows where both assigned_at and resolved_at are non-null.
Anchor the period on resolved_at (when the handling finished), and bound both ends.
Always return the sample size alongside the average — a 3-conversation average should not be reported as a trend.
Per-agent breakdown goes through (Conversation)-[:HANDLED_BY]->(Agent), returning Agent.display_name.
Email conversations skew AHT heavily. Split by c.channel before comparing periods.

name: SupportCase SLA Compliance
description: Share of resolved tickets that met resolution deadline (resolved_at <= due_at) or first-response deadline.
search_text: SupportCase SLA Compliance Share of resolved tickets that met resolution deadline (resolved_at <= due_at) or first-response deadline. (SupportCase)-[:GOVERNED_BY]->(ServiceLevelPolicy) matches on priority
